cards.title: Introduction to Flask Security
cards.content: Security is a critical aspect of web development. Flask provides the building blocks, but developers must implement robust measures to protect against vulnerabilities such as XSS, CSRF, and SQL Injection.

cards.title: Secure Password Hashing
cards.content:
Never store plain-text passwords. Use libraries like Werkzeug's security module to hash and check passwords securely.

from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash

hashd = generate_password_hash('secret')
is_correct = check_password_hash(hashd, 'secret')

cards.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cards.content: CSRF attacks trick the victim into submitting a malicious request. In Flask, extensions like Flask-WTF automatically handle CSRF tokens in forms to prevent this.

steps: User submits login form with username and password
Retrieve user record from the database
Log the user in by saving user ID in session

cards.title: Summary
cards.content: Always keep your dependencies updated, use HTTPS in production, never trust user input, and leverage built-in Flask extension security features.
